(2) the units of one stack or source share one record, so the specimen number labels the handled unit but cannot distinguish different properties, and each record covers that unit only; (3) the represented dimensions are shelterMeasure's ex21 rod law for wood and version-2 strand law for vine and reed, the mass of a whole plain unit is its represented unit mass, and partial units and worked or treated items have no represented geometry or mass reading; (4) a calibrated tool is any item or object carrying a complete, verified measurementCalibration record, trusted as declared provenance because only reviewed package code writes item records, and a condition below 0.75 (the shelter's sound threshold) is not serviceable; (5) readings round the represented value to the tool resolution, uncertainty adds the calibration uncertainty and half a graduation for each placement along the range (a conservative linear sum), and a pliable strand (flexibility at least 5) laid out straight by hand adds 1% of its reading; (6) a value below the resolution and a diameter or load beyond the range are found only while reading, so they are charged as a paid limit with no value; (7) tool readings need the light at which the ex19 checks see surfaces (above 0.1), while inspection is by handling and is paid in the dark with the visual traits unreported; (8) visible dryness bands of the represented water share are dry up to 0.4 (the shelter's and the world's air-dry grass), moist below 0.8 and wet from 0.8, and hand feel, for elongated pieces only, is stiff up to flexibility 3 (the ex21 rigidity limit), bends a little at 4 and pliable from 5 (the ex16 wrap limit); neither is reported as a number or used as a measurement; (9) the rod checks judge both ends of the uncertainty interval, a check failing at both ends is a measured failure, and rigidity, water share, pliability and strength stay unmeasurable, so the verdict is never suitable; (10) volume is an envelope cylinder with linear relative uncertainty, not a packed covering or bedding volume, and is not compared with the recipe's installed volumes; (11) a reading is current while the digest of the unit record (resource, origin, harvest time, quantity, composition, processing, decay, part condition and contact state, not position) is unchanged; (12) a hazard at a loose item or source makes it not safely accessible, and another person's carried items are not visible to the resolver. The installed capabilities are the forest, open and expression foundations, prepare-ventilated-food-storage@1, construct-weather-shelter@1, examine-material@1 and length-reference@1; examine-material records qualitative traits and calibrated dimensions, probe observe records visible state and its press, wet and heat trials consume material to test load, water or heat response, consult reads records, and eat is ingestion, so none tests a food hazard or preparation claim with detection limits, controls, hazards and disposal. Implemented (full specified scope, not a first release): assess-food-evidence@1 (ability and handler long.assess-food-evidence, equivalence food:specimen-evidence:non-ingestive-assessment:1, learning 2 at 0.2 energy per study round, 2.9 thousand code units, registered last, no visual component, no satisfaction source, one event food-evidence-assessed). assess: 1 round and 0.2 energy; target and specimen are examine-material@1's specimen (own item, loose item in reach or one unit in place in a source, not reserved, not under a hazard); evidenceRefs are at most four exact ids of complete records the person holds (a personal record key or its evidence event id, an eating record, a heard message id, or an earlier assessment); methodRef must be an installed capability or the person's record; equipmentRefs must be own items, loose items in reach or objects in reach; quantity is above 0 and at most one unit and is only recorded. Every malformed or inaccessible input, an unresolved reference, a paged fragment or undated record, a free-text method, too little energy or no study is refused before payment; an accessible specimen with no valid evidence or method is a paid assessment that yields the limitation report. It writes an unverified personal record (key target:unit-N:food-evidence, readable with consult) and an event with actor, target, unit, round and time, every cited id with its version (round, evidence event, content digest), the candidate protocol, equipment, conditions, applicability and currency checks, provenance (consult and probe of foundation-open@1, examine-material by its equivalence, as separate actions) and limitations. Direct observations (own unverified records of this target and unit, with their seen traits), validated findings (verified records about the same material, each scoped to its tested property and addressing no food question), unverified claims (the shown name of the target, visible signs about it, heard messages, records received from others) and unknowns (identity, the three questions, traits not seen when recorded, other units) are kept separate, and records about another material, source or unit, earlier assessments and stale records are listed as not applicable. Toxicity, edibility and preparation are reported independently, each unknown and unsupported with no claim, method, detection limit or uncertainty, and with what would support it; the conclusion is the specified one: no validated non-ingestive method established among supplied accessible evidence; toxicity, edibility and preparation requirements remain unknown, with absence of a result not a negative result and no claim that such a method cannot exist. The unmet requirements use the ex21 bill states: identification reference and validated protocol missing; equipment, controls, materials and safe conditions unestablished (set only by a validated method record); light missing in the dark; a calibrated balance missing for any measured-sample protocol. In the dark no new visual identification is made and earlier observations are cited as recorded, never as newly seen. execute-validated-method runs the same checks, then is refused before any cost, naming the candidate, the missing validated protocol, the number of installed capabilities checked and the nearest ones, and the unmet list; no sample, reagent or equipment is committed. Event view metadata: operation, mode, actor, target, unit, setting, status inconclusive, progress, rounds, evidence refs, method, conditions, result unknown, uncertainty, limitation codes dark and missing-method, prior observations, newlySeen empty, badge, assay, tools, reagents and samples empty or null, position and evidence; no safe-food badge, assay or preparation effect. Request: at round 73 Sol (health 100, satiety 86.3, energy 40) asked for an operation that eats a specified whole-unit quantity of a specified food resource from owned stacks, the oldest harvested stack first and ties broken by exact item id, because eat with target resource:berry had failed as ambiguous while Sol held three berry stacks and a repeating plan cannot name item ids gathered later. World Agent decision: develop (learning 1) only a deterministic owned-stack selector that delegates the eating to the existing eat (foundation-forest@1, handler forest.eat), not a replacement nutrition or food-safety system. Implemented: eat-oldest-owned-food@1 (ability and handler long.eat-oldest-owned-food, equivalence food:owned-stack:oldest-harvested-first-eat:1, learning 1 at 0.2 study energy, 2.3 thousand code units, registered last, dependencies foundation-forest@1 and the eat interface, no visual component, no satisfaction source, one event oldest-food-stack-eaten). Arguments: resource as resource:ID under the shared reference spelling policy (surrounding and prefix whitespace accepted, never another id; item ids and bare names are malformed) and quantity with the eat schema (integer, at least 1). Selection, at each execution: the person's own stacks of exactly that resource that are unreserved, pass the owned-reference resolution eat itself runs on an exact item id (so personally accessible) and each hold the whole quantity alone, sorted by harvestedAt ascending with missing values last, then by exact item id in code-unit order; the first is chosen. One stack only, as the specification requires: stacks are never combined, so a quantity no single stack holds is refused with nothing eaten and no remainder, and no resource is substituted, gathered or judged safe. Consumption: the forest.eat handler is called with interface eat, the chosen exact id and the quantity, as other packages call base handlers, so validation, nutrition, toxicity and injury, the satiety cap, food condition and meal quality, the discoveries record, meal experience, the ate event and failures are all those of eat; an eat refusal (for example of an owned branch) is passed through with the chosen id at no cost. Costs: exactly the delegated eat, one round, its meal energy (stated as 1 and scaled by mood inside eat) and the units eaten; the selection adds no time, energy or material. Duration and continuity: one atomic round like eat; nothing is reserved, held, paused or released, a refused or interrupted round commits nothing, and each use, including each repeat of a plan step, resolves again. Free refusals before any cost: malformed-resource; no-matching-owned-stock (no usable owned stack of it, including when every one is reserved by ongoing work); no-single-stack-with-requested-quantity (usable stacks exist but none holds the quantity alone); unstudied use and a missing eat dependency are refused by the kernel. Refusal texts name only the resource and quantity, never candidate ids or anyone else's stock. Event: oldest-food-stack-eaten after the delegated ate event, with actor, resource, requested quantity, the chosen item (a selected list of one), its harvest round, the ordering rule, consumed quantity, outcome eaten and the delegated eat revision with its ate event id, plus nested view metadata (operation, phase completed, actor, resource, item, quantity, consumed quantity, progress 1, outcome eaten), so no top-level progress field marks the meal as work; other candidates stay private, and the outcome text keeps the satiety report of eat. Happiness: no reward; the event never carries a qualified flag, so no practice milestone or satisfaction follows, and study grants nothing. Migration: none; installation adds only the ability and the event type. Visual review: no new component; ordinary eating visuals come from the ate event of eat and committed stack changes, and a refusal emits only the kernel failed event with no eating effect. Known difference outside this scope: the routine-burden record counts eat as a survival routine by its interface name, so a meal through this operation is logged as a non-routine round (it never marks progress either), and like every extension event the completion event enters the person's important-event list while a plain ate event does not; aligning either needs a revision-gated change to a shared runtime file, which this handoff excludes. What Sol can do now: study for one round (0.2 energy), then eat resource:berry with quantity 1 without naming an item. A throwaway check on the archived round-73 world, in memory only, mastered it for 0.2 energy, ate item-69-sol-772 (Sol's only berry stack by then) with satiety 85.4 to 92.5 and energy 39.8 to 38.80123365, identical to eating that item directly, chose item-56-sol-642, the earliest of four root stacks, for resource:root, and refused resource:berry with quantity 2, resource:hazelnut and a bare berry at no cost. Assumptions: (1) ordinary eat targeting prerequisites are the owned-reference resolution eat runs plus its quantity check, while edibility stays the check of eat itself; (2) no matching owned stock means no usable owned stack, reserved stacks counting as unusable; (3) eat is atomic, so the escrow, interruption, death and pause rules of the specification have nothing to hold; (4) the ate event this action emits for the chosen item reports the meal.
